note: Case list for tools/chart_parity.py — the Phase B Flip A parity gate.
Each case is a URL for the headless /r/chart route: a committed bar fixture
(`fixedbars`), one chart preset, and a PARTIAL chart_settings blob describing
exactly the indicator under test. The harness base64url-encodes preset+settings
into ?indicators= and screenshots the #chart-export element on two builds.
A case may also carry `instancesB`: a list of ENGINE indicator instances sent
as `?instances=` to side B only (`--instances-side` moves it to both/neither).
That is how one build renders the same indicator two ways — legacy on A, engine
on B — so the diff measures the migration rather than two checkouts of the app.
The four live cases are the Flip A pilot. The rest are NAME-ONLY placeholders:
B3 fills in each one's settings blob when it migrates that indicator, so the
list already states the full obligation instead of quietly shrinking to what
was easy. `--include-placeholders` runs them; the default run skips them.
Tolerance is 0 everywhere and should stay 0 — see report.md's 'Reading this'.
A per-case `tolerance` must be accompanied by `toleranceReason`.
DO NOT change `defaults.fixedbars`, `w`, `h` or the preset without re-capturing
every stored baseline: they are part of what a baseline PNG means.

classic_flat._why: The 'Classic Dark' preset (= CHART_DEFAULTS) with the four MA overlays and the watermark removed, so the indicator under test is the dominant ink on the canvas and a diff is attributable to it rather than to an EMA that happens to cross it. Volume keeps its own pane because a pane-count change is itself a regression worth catching.

cases.name: bb_only
cases.why: LEGACY vs LEGACY. Both sides draw the three bands through the hand-written StockChart block, so this is the determinism case for a price overlay and the flag-OFF regression case for any commit that touches the BB block. The legacy-vs-ENGINE measurement is `engine_bb_vs_legacy`.

cases.name: rsi_only
cases.why: Single-line separate pane — proves pane creation, height and the 30/70 guides survive the move.

cases.name: macd_only
cases.why: Three outputs in one pane, one of them a sign-coloured histogram. The B1 note in indicators.js says StockChart masks the MACD line's head back to the signal's first bar — this case is what proves that mask is still there.

cases.name: macd_headmask
cases.why: MEASURES A DECISION, NOT A MIGRATION (B3/A5, decision id MACD_HEAD_MASK — APPLIED 2026-08-02, the mask was DROPPED). Run it between a build with `nativeRegistry.MACD_HEAD_MASK = false` (what ships today) and one with it true (the pre-2026-08-02 look) — the ONLY case in this file whose two sides differ by a source constant rather than by a checkout or a URL parameter. The number is what it costs to draw the mathematically-correct MACD line from bar slowPeriod-1 instead of holding its head back to the signal's first bar: 8 bars (25..32) at 12/26/9, which is what the Python lane and `tests/fixtures/indicators/macd_default.json` both publish and this chart now draws. A `fixedbars` fixture of 200 daily bars puts those 8 bars at the far left of the visible range, which is exactly where a user would notice. MEASURED 88 px (0.011828%), 20/20 runs, zero variance, both before the decision and again at the flip; one contiguous 44x4 px region at x in [136,179], y in [394,397]. Expected NON-ZERO — and post-flip a ZERO means something worse than theatre: BOTH lanes read this one constant, and `macd` is NOT migrated, so a 0 means a future edit stopped one of them reading it and the lane users see is out of step with the engine. Settings are byte-identical to `macd_only` on purpose — that case is the legacy-vs-legacy determinism baseline for the same picture, so the two together separate 'the mask moved' from 'the renderer wobbled'. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2026-08-02-macd-head-mask.md`.

cases.name: bb_rsi_macd
cases.why: All three at once: an overlay plus TWO extra panes. Catches pane-ordering and pane-height regressions that no single-indicator case can see.

cases.name: engine_rsi_vs_legacy
cases.why: THE DARK REHEARSAL. Side A draws RSI through the hand-written StockChart block; side B draws it through the ENGINE (`instancesB` → `?instances=`, which also arms `engineEnabled`), and StockChart's per-indicator ownership check stands the legacy block down so exactly ONE RSI line exists on each side. Same build, same fixture, one URL parameter apart — so a non-zero diff is the migration and nothing else. `indicators.rsi.enabled` stays TRUE on both sides on purpose: `computePaneMargins` reads it, and it is what reserves the identical band for the engine to render into.

cases.name: engine_rsi_toggle_off
cases.why: THE FLIP-A SWITCH, IN PIXELS. `indicators.rsi.enabled` is FALSE on both sides, and side B additionally hands the engine an RSI instance. StockChart projects an instance whose legacy toggle is off to `hidden`, so the engine must draw NOTHING and the two sides must be the same bare chart. Without this case the projection is gated only in jsdom, and the specific regression it catches is the one that produced this branch's worst bug: a band that is not reserved (computePaneMargins reads the same flag) while a line is still drawn, which `resolvePlacement` then falls back to {top:0.82,bottom:0} — ON TOP OF THE VOLUME BARS.
cases._history: Written in Task 2's fix round, measured at 24 px on 3 runs in 5, and DELETED on the reading that it was 'an A-vs-B work asymmetry / capture timing'. That diagnosis was WRONG, and deleting the case removed the evidence rather than the cause. Re-measured 2026-08-02 over 40 runs with the hardened harness (every capture proven pixel-stable before it was accepted, 2 shots on all 80): the 24 px is a BISTABLE RASTERISATION OF THE DASHED LAST-PRICE LINE, one row, ~12 dash boundaries, and it appears INDEPENDENTLY on both sides (legacy side 5/40, engine side 7/40) with no correlation to settle time. Sides A and B draw the same two images with the same frequencies, so it is not an asymmetry and not the migration — it is Chromium rasterising one dashed line two ways at this pane geometry. The other three engine cases were byte-identical across all 80 captures.
cases._priceLineReason: ⚠️ NOT A TOLERANCE. The last-price line is drawn by the CANDLE series; no case measures it and it is identical on both sides by construction. `priceLine: false` removes a provably nondeterministic ELEMENT from this one case — the same treatment the footer's wall-clock stamp gets under ?fixedbars= — and the case must still report 0 on every run. The three cases that are already byte-identical keep the line, deliberately: their stored baselines mean what they meant before.

cases.name: engine_bb_vs_legacy
cases.why: THE FIRST PRICE OVERLAY. Side A draws the three Bollinger lines through the hand-written StockChart block; side B draws them through the ENGINE. This is the case that measures the `autoscaleInfoProvider` seam: without it the bands drag the CANDLES' autoscale and the whole price pane re-scales, which is a whole-canvas diff (38,491 px, 343 rows x 1,160 columns), not a line-width one. It also measures the C-2 fix (`priceScaleId` named rather than omitted) on a create. IT DOES NOT MEASURE THE ENGINE CALL SITE'S POSITION, and it used to claim it did: the `classic_flat` preset sets `overlays: []` and `volume.separatePane: true`, so pane 0 holds only the candles and BB, nothing crosses anything, and moving the sync call produces 0 px. `engine_bb_over_overlays` is the case that earns that claim; the jsdom rail for it is `stockChartWiring.test.jsx`'s z-order pair.

cases.name: engine_bb_over_overlays
cases.why: THE CASE THAT EARNS THE CALL-SITE CLAIM. `engine_bb_vs_legacy` runs on the `classic_flat` preset, whose `overlays: []` and `volume.separatePane: true` leave pane 0 holding only the candles and BB — nothing crosses anything, so moving the engine sync call site produces 0 px there and the claim was unearned. This case turns the four MA overlays ON and brings volume INTO pane 0, so pane 0 really does contain volume bars, five moving averages and three Bollinger lines, and INSERTION ORDER IS Z-ORDER (lightweight-charts appends and paints by ascending zorder). Side A draws BB through the legacy block, side B through the engine, and the engine's sync must land in the same place the legacy block did: after volume and the MA overlays, before the first legacy indicator. Move it and the bands paint UNDER the overlays instead of over them. The jsdom rail for the same claim is `stockChartWiring.test.jsx`'s z-order pair; this is the pixel half. Expected 0 px, like every Flip A case — MEASURED 0 on 5/5, build 54443afee3e3, one build two ways. AND IT IS NOT A VACUOUS 0: with the sync call site moved up above the volume and MA blocks (the R12 shape, engine on BOTH sides, builds 54443afee3e3 vs bea40b9aec38) this case reports 281 px on 3/3 across 86 rows and 206 columns, while `engine_bb_vs_legacy` reports 0 on the same mutation — which is exactly why this case exists.

cases.name: engine_bb_rsi_vs_legacy
cases.why: THE PILOT PAIR TOGETHER. A price overlay and a banded oscillator in one render, which is the only case that can see the engine drawing its series contiguously where legacy interleaves them, and the only one where a pooled series can cross between the two placement paths within a single sync.
